meta.purpose: Facts about Wikidata's RDF and the endpoints that the explanation rules (SPEC §4) rely on. Each fact has a source and a verification status.

status_values.verbatim: checked against the source's own text (raw wikitext or page text)
status_values.partial: part checked verbatim, part from a secondary summary or inference; see note
status_values.corpus: observed in this corpus / rewriter output, not in documentation

F-RANK.fact: wdt: (truthy) triples exist only for statements with the best non-deprecated rank for that property: preferred statements if any exist, otherwise all normal-rank statements. Deprecated statements never produce wdt: triples. Qualifiers are ignored.
F-RANK.quote: Truthy statements represent statements that have the best non-deprecated rank for a given property. ... if there is a preferred statement for property P2, then only preferred statements for P2 will be considered truthy. Otherwise, all normal-rank statements for P2 are considered truthy.

F-RANK-VALUES.fact: Every statement node has wikibase:rank, one of wikibase:NormalRank, wikibase:PreferredRank, wikibase:DeprecatedRank. Best-rank statements also have type wikibase:BestRank.
F-RANK-VALUES.quote: The statement rank is represented by the predicate wikibase:rank and the object being one of: wikibase:NormalRank, wikibase:PreferredRank, wikibase:DeprecatedRank.

F-PS-UNIQUE.fact: A statement node has exactly one main value (ps:) — or, for novalue, none.
F-PS-UNIQUE.source: RDF §Statement representation; DM (a Statement has one main Snak)
F-PS-UNIQUE.note: Follows from the data model (one main snak per statement); not quoted verbatim yet.

F-SOMEVALUE.fact: 'Unknown value' appears as a value in both the truthy (wdt:) and full (ps:) forms. In the dump it is a blank node; WDQS uses Skolem IRIs instead. So `?x wdt:P []` and `?x wdt:P ?v` match unknown values.
F-SOMEVALUE.quote: Unknown value is represented as RDF blank node in both simplified and full statements: wd:Q3 a wikibase:Item, wdt:P2 _:genid1 . | WDQS now uses local IRIs (Skolem IRIs) instead of blank nodes to represent somevalue.
F-SOMEVALUE.corpus_note: The Factoidal (and Wikimedia) rewriter recognises them by the text 'wikidata.org/.well-known/genid' (rule rewrite-wikibase-isSomeValue). That the target QLever endpoint uses the same form is assumed from the rewriter, not documented here.

F-NOVALUE.fact: 'No value' is not a value: it is a class (wdno:P) on the item or statement. It produces no wdt: or ps: value, so `?x wdt:P []` does not match it.
F-NOVALUE.quote: Novalue is represented not by a regular value but as a class of the entity or statement or reference, with prefix wdno: and the name of the property. ... Note that wdno:P22 mentioned above is not a predicate, unlike others, but a class.

F-LABEL-UNIQUE.fact: For any language, an entity has at most one label and at most one description, but any number of aliases.
F-LABEL-UNIQUE.quote: for any given language, an EntityDescription may have at most one label and at most one description, but any number of aliases.

F-LABEL-PREDICATE.fact: In WDQS, labels are stored only as rdfs:label (the dump also has schema:name and skos:prefLabel). Aliases are skos:altLabel; descriptions are schema:description; all are language-tagged literals.
F-LABEL-PREDICATE.quote: For labels, only rdfs:label is stored but not schema:name or skos:prefLabel.
F-LABEL-PREDICATE.note: QLever's Wikidata index is assumed to follow WDQS here; not checked.

F-MUL.fact: 'mul' is a language code for default labels and aliases that apply across languages. It is used for labels and aliases; descriptions are not covered (a separate solution is planned).
F-MUL.quote: These default values can be accessed via API using the language code mul ("multiple languages"). | a different solution is in the works for descriptions (see T303677)
F-MUL.note: Read via fetch tool, not raw wikitext. Consistent with the corpus: the Factoidal rewrite adds 'mul' for labels, never descriptions.

F-SITELINK-UNIQUE.fact: An item has at most one sitelink per wiki.
F-SITELINK-UNIQUE.quote: Note that while an Item can have multiple sitelinks to different wikis, it cannot have multiple sitelinks to the same wiki.

F-SITELINK-RDF.fact: A sitelink is a node of type schema:Article (its IRI is the article URL), linked to the entity by schema:about, with schema:isPartOf <wiki root URL>, schema:inLanguage "code", schema:name (the title), and wikibase:badge for each badge.
F-SITELINK-RDF.quote: The type of the node is schema:Article and it linked with the entity via schema:about predicate. Badges are described with wikibase:badge predicates. schema:name predicate holds the plain-text name of the article, in the language of the linked wiki.
F-SITELINK-RDF.note: schema:isPartOf and schema:inLanguage are shown in the example, not described in prose.

F-REDIRECT.fact: A redirected entity is recorded as `old owl:sameAs target`. WDQS gives this no further meaning: data is stored on the target, so a query naming the old ID matches only the owl:sameAs triple.
F-REDIRECT.quote: Redirected entities are implemented as owl:sameAs predicates ... wd:Q6 owl:sameAs wd:Q1 . | Redirects are recorded but currently have no additional semantics implemented.

F-DATE-PRECISION.fact: Every date has a precision: 11 day, 10 month, 9 year, 8 decade, 7 century, 6 millennium. The truthy (wdt:) value is a plain xsd:dateTime with no precision, so a date known only to the year still looks like a full date; its precision is only on the full value (wikibase:timePrecision).
F-DATE-PRECISION.quote: Precision table: 11 day, 10 month, 9 year, 8 decade, 7 century, 6 millennium. | Precisions higher than 11 (day) are not supported as of 2021.
F-DATE-PRECISION.note: How a year-precision date's month and day appear in RDF (01-01 vs 00-00) was seen only in a summary. The JSON form uses 00-00. Before rendering any claim about month or day placeholders, check RDF output directly.

F-DATE-BCE.fact: RDF dates use XSD 1.1 year numbering (1 BCE is year 0), so BCE years in RDF are offset by one from the conventional year.
F-DATE-BCE.note: Seen only in a summary; verify before use.

F-LABEL-FALLBACK.fact: In WDQS, the label service gives the entity ID (e.g. Q123) when no label exists in any requested language. The Factoidal rewrite reproduces this explicitly (strafter(str(?x), "entity/")).
F-LABEL-FALLBACK.quote: If no label is available in any of the specified languages, the Q-id of the entity (without any prefix) is its label.
F-LABEL-FALLBACK.note: Read via fetch tool, not raw wikitext.

F-GEODIST-UNIT.fact: geof:distance returns kilometres: on WDQS always, and on QLever by default (QLever accepts an optional third unit argument, which the Factoidal rewrite drops).
F-GEODIST-UNIT.quote: The function geof:distance returns distance between two points on Earth, in kilometers. (WDQS) | If no unit is given, the distance is returned in kilometers. (QLever docs, per search result summary)
F-GEODIST-UNIT.note: The QLever wording comes from a search summary; read docs.qlever.dev/geosparql/ before treating it as verbatim.

F-HIERARCHY-PROPS.fact: Properties usually read transitively, where a direct match omits things linked through intermediate values: P131 (located in the administrative territorial entity), P361 (part of), P279 (subclass of), P171 (parent taxon), P276 (location).
F-HIERARCHY-PROPS.source: editorial: project convention, not a Wikidata rule
F-HIERARCHY-PROPS.note: Policy list for R-DIRECT-ONLY. Review and extend by hand; this is a judgment, not a fact about the data.
